content.title: About
content.content: Knockwurst is a traditional German boiled‑then‑grilled sausage made from pork and veal, seasoned with paprika, nutmeg and other spices. It has a tender pink hue, a mild smoky aroma and a gently spicy bite.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Knockwurst originated in Berlin in the late 19th century as a quick street snack for laborers.
The name derives from the German word "Knock", referring to the light tapping butchers used to test the sausage’s firmness.
Traditionally the sausage is simmered in water at about 80 °C before being quickly seared on a grill.
In the United States it became popular in German immigrant communities and is often served with mustard and sauerkraut.
There is a vegetarian version made from soy protein and spices.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Knockwurst provides roughly 12 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for normal blood formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: The iron in meat is highly bioavailable and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: Provides zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune health and wound healing.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: With less than 2 g of carbs per 100 g, knockwurst fits well into low‑carb diets.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pork or veal.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Knockwurst is often salty; people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands contain nitrites, which can be harmful in excess.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Fatty meat products may cause gastrointestinal upset in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve knockwurst hot, sliced, with mustard, sauerkraut or potato salad. It also works well in stews, soups, and as a sandwich filling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep knockwurst refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container for up to 5 days. For longer storage freeze at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 3 months. Before use, check for off‑odors or discoloration.
